defn: A framework from Dave Snowden that sorts situations into clear, complicated, complex and chaotic. Each needs a different way of acting.
Working out together what's going on in an unclear situation, before deciding what to do.
When the result of an action loops back and shapes the next action.
Ashby's law: to steer something, your responses need to be at least as varied as the situations you face.
About steering through feedback, in machines, living things or organizations.
A small experiment designed so that if it fails, the damage is small and you still learn.
When a whole shows patterns that none of its parts have on their own.
Designing a service end to end: what people experience and the behind-the-scenes work that makes it happen.
A diagram of a service showing what users see, and the backstage work behind each step.
A picture of the steps someone goes through to get something done, and how each step feels.
Lou Downe's plain-language standards for what makes a service work well for the people using it.
Learning directly from the people who use a service: watching, asking, testing.
